solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Adhesive as once used to fill stain

indicators.note: to fill something is to go inside it, so one word's letters sit within the other's

blocks.note: to black is to stain or blacken
ut is an obsolete word for 'as', from Latin

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a sticky substance that was once used to fill a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' tells you the word for 'as' is archaic. Blu-Tack is a reusable putty-like adhesive brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Blu-Tack is a trade name for a putty used to stick posters to walls, so it is a kind of adhesive.

clue.text: Qualified lawyer, subordinate plonker? It could be fatal

blocks.note: BL is Bachelor of Laws
under means lower in rank
in Chambers a plonker is a big wet kiss, and buss is a kiss

explanation.surface: A law graduate calls a junior colleague an idiot, which could be deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plonker' is British slang for a fool, but here it is the rarer sense of a smacking kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunderbuss is an old short gun with a flared muzzle, and a weapon can cause death.

clue.text: Malagasy native? Supporter of La Maison probably

blocks.note: first meaning: an animal found only in Madagascar
second meaning: French for 'the wall', which holds up a house

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as two French words, the wall, which is what probably holds up la maison, the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are primates native only to Madagascar, whose people and things are called Malagasy.

clue.text: Traffic in Glasgow? Reduced it with firm support

indicators.note: something reduced is cut down, so a letter of the next word is lost

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut down
a rock is something solid to rely on

explanation.surface: Glasgow's traffic eased by solid backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Glasgow' marks a Scots word; 'traffic' is the verb to trade, not road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Trock is Scots for to barter or deal, which is the sense of traffic as trading.

clue.text: Camion requiring service, indicating a sort of breakdown

indicators.note: something needing a service must be taken apart and reworked, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; a camion is a heavy lorry

explanation.surface: A lorry needs servicing, a sign that it has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: The breakdown is social, not mechanical.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomic means relating to anomie, the collapse of social norms and values in a society.

clue.text: Mobile home needing attention. Dry after a fan installed

indicators.note: something installed is fitted inside, so these letters go within the attention word

blocks.note: care is attention
taken as written
a vane is a blade of a fan, or a winnowing fan
TT means teetotal, in crossword terms dry

explanation.surface: A camper van needs some attention: dry it out once a fan is fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the teetotal letters behind the fan before the lot goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravanette is a motor caravan, a vehicle with living quarters that serves as a home on wheels.

clue.text: Carpenter's tool, not so complicated, I got rid of

indicators.note: getting rid of a thing removes it, so a letter is taken out of the word

blocks.note: plainer means simpler, less complicated
the letter I as written, the one removed

explanation.surface: A carpenter boasts of a simpler tool, having discarded something.
explanation.definitionFit: A planer is a machine or hand tool that smooths wood, used by a carpenter.

clue.text: Attitude of some Greek islands, about depth of deity ruling their surroundings

indicators.note: about means around, so the islands wrap round the single letter

blocks.note: a pose is an attitude or posture
the Ionian Islands lie off western Greece
d is the abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: A survey of the posture of Greek islands and the sea god around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Their surroundings' are the seas round the islands, which Poseidon ruled.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidonian means relating to Poseidon, the Greek god who governs the sea.

clue.text: Walk round lake? It's familiar to geneticist

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the path goes about the single letter

blocks.note: an allée is a tree-lined walk or avenue
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A scientist strolls round a lake that they know well.
explanation.definitionFit: An allele is one of the alternative forms of a gene, a term every geneticist uses.

clue.text: Hitmen in Japan? One among that lot

indicators.note: among that lot points back to the preceding words, within which the letters sit

blocks.note: the run from the end of hitmen through the start of Japan

explanation.surface: Someone asks about Japanese assassins and points to one of the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hitmen in Japan' does double duty: the letters are there, and it defines the answer, whose plural is unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninja were feudal Japanese agents trained in stealth and assassination, hired killers in effect.

clue.text: Business on the up? Number involved enter thrustingly as before

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is written bottom to top
involved means wrapped in, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: trade is business
n is the symbol for a number

explanation.surface: A business is thriving, with numbers forcefully coming in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks an archaic word, here Spenserian.
explanation.definitionFit: Endart is an obsolete verb meaning to dart in, that is to pierce or penetrate.

clue.text: Rock record tenet: 'Backing required'

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so the letters that follow are disturbed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rock band's principle about its record: support is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like the music genre, and 'Backing' like a band's support; one is the anagram signal, the other the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrocedent means moving or going back, as a disease that recedes, so it means going in reverse.

clue.text: What needs to be held in both hands for oven

indicators.note: something held in another's grasp sits inside it, so the letters go within the pair

blocks.note: signals that one letter comes from each hand
L and R, the left and right hands
eh? is an interjection meaning what?

explanation.surface: A cook wonders what must be carried in both hands to go in the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: A lehr is a long annealing furnace in which glass is cooled slowly, a specialised oven.

clue.text: Rope aboard sailing vessel mostly trundling east

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the next word is dropped

blocks.note: trundling a ball is bowling it
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A rope on board a ship that is mostly rolling eastward.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowline is a rope on a square-rigged ship used to keep the edge of a sail steady into the wind.

clue.text: Backing band includes knight, rather hard up

indicators.note: to include is to hold inside, so one part sits within the other
backing means going backwards, so the whole assembly is read from right to left

blocks.note: a hoop is a band, as round a barrel
Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: A band supporting a knighted musician is short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Poorish means somewhat poor, which is to be rather short of money.

clue.text: Goblin with twitchy ears, an old gnome?

indicators.note: something twitchy jerks about restlessly, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: an imp is a goblin or small devil
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is a goblin with nervous ears an old garden gnome?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnome' means a maxim here, not a garden ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresa was a heraldic device with a motto, and a gnome is a pithy maxim or saying.

clue.text: Spicy sauce got from can mum cooked with duck (7, two words)

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A spicy sauce made from what's in a tin that mother cooked with a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuoc mam is the pungent Vietnamese fish sauce used as a seasoning, a spicy condiment.

clue.text: Something akin to a swift beer towards closing time?

definitions.text: Something akin to a swift beer towards closing time?

blocks.clueFragment: Something akin to a swift beer towards closing time?
blocks.note: surface reading: a quick pint gulped down just before the pub shuts
setter's reading: a bird related to the swift, whose dialect name splits as evening plus a jar of beer

explanation.walkthrough: A swift is also a bird; 'a jar' is British slang for a drink of beer, and towards closing time is evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The evejar is a dialect name for the nightjar, a nocturnal bird resembling swifts in shape and habits.

clue.text: Coming round tinker duly bags such rubbish

indicators.note: to bag is to hold inside, so the run of letters is held within these words
coming round means turning about, so the concealed letters read right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of tinker and the start of duly

explanation.surface: A tinker making his rounds properly collects junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Drek is a Yiddish-derived word for trash or worthless stuff.

clue.text: Stop dropping in for a mild smoke

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: a clarion is an organ stop
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop popping in just for a light cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' reads as a command but is the noun, an organ stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A claro is a light-coloured, mild cigar, so it is a gentle smoke.

clue.text: Being abandoned, didn't scream, though upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone left behind kept quiet despite being distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Discardment is the state of being discarded, that is of having been cast aside or deserted.

clue.text: Onset of disease in the early wheat, causing stir in Scotland

indicators.note: the onset is the start, so only the first letter is used
in means placed inside, so the letter goes within the grain

blocks.note: durum is a hard wheat
the first letter of disease

explanation.surface: Disease appearing in the young wheat caused an uproar among Scottish farmers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early' simply suggests an old type of wheat; 'in Scotland' marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Durdum is Scots for an uproar or commotion, so it means a stir or fuss.

clue.text: Being unwell shifty 'ob's kept inside

indicators.note: kept inside means held within, so this piece goes within the other

blocks.note: sly means shifty, untrustworthy
a hob is a rustic, a hick; the apostrophe drops the H in the same way

explanation.surface: A dodgy character feels poorly while his oven hob is shut in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cockney dropped H in 'ob tells you to drop the H of its synonym too.
explanation.definitionFit: Sickly describes someone in poor health or ailing, which is the state of being ill.

clue.text: What's anathema to vegans, useless as opening

blocks.note: vegans do not eat meat
US stands for unserviceable, that is useless

explanation.surface: Something vegans loathe seen as a pointless opener.
explanation.definitionFit: A meatus is an anatomical passage or opening, such as the canal of the ear.

clue.text: Source of dye I added to massage, first- class?

blocks.note: to massage is to rub
taken as written
A is a first-class grade

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a dye that came with a massage is top quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read in a different order from the clue: the massage word comes first, then I, then the top grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubia is the madder genus of plants, whose roots were long a source of red dye.

clue.text: Aussie plonk, ordinary accompanying local banger

blocks.note: in Australia a bomb is an old car, which the British call a banger
O is the abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: Cheap Australian wine served with a sausage from the area.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger looks like a sausage, but here it is a decrepit car; 'local' follows on from 'Aussie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombo is Australian slang for cheap wine, which plonk also means.

clue.text: Five kept in enclosure, often spare

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so one letter goes within the others

blocks.note: an SAE, stamped addressed envelope, is often enclosed with a letter
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five things are often kept in a pen as surplus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enclosure' looks like a pen or field; it is what goes in an envelope with a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To spare someone is to save them from harm, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Helping of kirschwasser? It ends with one

definitions.note: the clue word ends in this sound

indicators.note: a helping is a portion of a dish, so only part of the next word is taken

blocks.note: the letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: Someone takes a glass of cherry brandy and notes how it finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back: kirschwasser, said in English, ends in this sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A schwa is the neutral unstressed vowel sound, as at the end of the German spirit's name.

clue.text: When it's getting late, everything imbibed in it is toxic stuff

indicators.note: only what is drunk inside the word is kept, so its outside letters are dropped

blocks.note: evening is the time of day when it grows late

explanation.surface: Late in the day, whatever is drunk in it is poisonous.
explanation.definitionFit: Venin is a toxin found in snake venom, so it is a poisonous substance.

clue.text: Soft loaf I cut with raised pattern

indicators.note: cut means removed, so that letter is taken out of the bread

blocks.note: a brioche is a soft sweet French loaf
taken as written, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A baker trims a soft loaf with a raised design.
explanation.definitionFit: Broché describes fabric woven with a raised figure or design, as in brocade.

clue.text: Grabbed a bite in the office? Tin rolled over in desk messily

indicators.note: something rolled over is turned upside down, so this word reads backwards
done messily means out of order, so these letters are scrambled
in means placed inside, so one part sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a can is a tin

explanation.definitionFit: To have snacked is to have eaten a light quick meal, which is grabbing a bite.

clue.text: Female imbibing a wee bittie Scotch where the sailors tie up

indicators.note: imbibing means taking in, so the small amount goes inside the female

tait is a Scots word for a small amount

explanation.surface: A woman sips a little Scotch whisky at the quayside where sailors moor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky but tells you the word for a little bit is Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: A staithe is a landing stage or wharf, a place where boats are moored to load and unload.

clue.text: Deny extra editing work on the paper may keep this?

blocks.note: a sub, substitute, is an extra or reserve

blocks.clueFragment: editing work on the paper may keep this?
blocks.note: newspaper sub-editing often keeps staff at work late

explanation.surface: Someone denies that extra editorial work on a newspaper might hold this.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint: sub-editors on a paper often work late into the night.
explanation.definitionFit: In logic and philosophy, to sublate is to negate or contradict a proposition.

clue.text: Mark refuses tot initially – being on it? (Charles has one)

definitions.note: the thing one is on: refusing a tot means being on the wagon

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted
refusing something means turning it away, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: Mark Twain, the American author
the first letter of tot
a confirming aside, not wordplay

explanation.surface: A teetotal Mark turns down a dram; King Charles has a wagon too.
explanation.walkthrough: Refusing a tot means being on the wagon. Charles's Wain is an old British name for the Plough constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: A wain is a wagon, and Charles's Wain is the star pattern also called the Plough or Big Dipper.

clue.text: Expression of pleasure no longer shown by Mosley being banged up

definitions.text: Expression of pleasure no longer shown

indicators.note: something banged up is battered and knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Oswald Mosley, the British fascist leader, was jailed in wartime and showed no more pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: Mosley was interned during the Second World War, which makes 'banged up', British slang for imprisoned, apt.

clue.text: Deny sanctity of a nun? It's out of order

indicators.note: out of order means not in the proper sequence, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether disowning a nun's holiness is improper.
